page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge is a GPU-accelerated server instance powered by an Intel Xeon E5-2682 v4 processor operating at 2.5 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the instance delivers 8 vCPUs across 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, alongside a 40 MB L3 cache. The system is provisioned with 32 GB of system memory, allocating 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Hardware acceleration is provided by a single dedicated NVIDIA Pascal architecture P4 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM. This instance features a 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile and includes no local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring persistent disk operations to be handled by attached cloud storage.

Benchmark testing demonstrates modest processing capabilities typical of previous-generation hardware. Single-core stress-ng tests recorded a score of 953.38, while multi-core performance reached 4755.08. PassMark CPU tests yielded a total score of 6698.53, and uncached memory bandwidth registered at 37.18 GB/sec for read operations and 25.34 GB/sec for write operations. These metrics reflect the capabilities of the Broadwell-era Intel architecture and placing overall CPU and memory bandwidth performance in lower tiers compared to modern cloud hardware.

In terms of qualitative cost efficiency, the ecs.gn5i-c8g1.2xlarge serves as a budget-conscious entry point for workloads that require dedicated NVIDIA GPU capabilities without requiring high compute overhead. The integration of the low-power NVIDIA P4 GPU makes the instance effective for legacy AI inference, low-density computer vision, and video stream encoding. However, the lack of local disk storage and limited CPU single-thread performance make it less suitable for disk-bound database applications or compute-heavy modern deep learning training pipelines.

Hardware acceleration is delivered via a single integrated NVIDIA P4 GPU with 8 GB of VRAM based on the Pascal architecture. The instance is designed for cost-conscious, low-density GPU workloads such as light machine learning inference, legacy media transcoding, and specialized computer vision pipelines where baseline hardware acceleration is needed without heavy compute throughput demands.
